title: The carbon fatty acid synthesis throws away

scenes.tts: Why does a cell pay to attach carbon dioxide, only to throw it away two steps later? That apparent waste is the trick that makes fatty acid synthesis move forward.
scenes.caption: Why does a cell pay to attach CO₂, only to throw it away two steps later? That apparent waste is the trick that makes fatty acid synthesis move forward.
scenes.visual: Open inside a dark, schematic cytoplasm with one large assembly machine filling the frame. A two-carbon acetyl CoA block rolls toward an ACC gate; an ATP coin turns the gate, a bright CO2 badge clips onto the block, then hangs over an exit chute. During the question, the block rocks between the gate and chute while a short label, ‘Why add, then discard?’, grows above it. Keep belts, gate gears and small background particles moving throughout. No molecular structures.
scenes.narration: Why does a cell pay to attach CO₂, only to throw it away two steps later? That apparent waste is the trick that makes fatty acid synthesis move forward.

scenes.visual: Keep the same moving assembly floor. Dim the gate without stopping its gears, center the attached CO2 badge and block, and reveal the title ‘The carbon fatty acid synthesis throws away’ in two large lines. The conveyor continues creeping beneath the title.

scenes.tts: In its simplest form, begin with acetyl C O A already in the cytoplasm. Its two carbons are the primer. Every later pair enters through malonyl C O A, the extender made by acetyl C O A carboxylase, or A C C.
scenes.caption: In its simplest form, begin with acetyl CoA already in the cytoplasm. Its two carbons are the primer. Every later pair enters through malonyl CoA, the extender made by acetyl CoA carboxylase, or ACC.
scenes.visual: Return the title to the upper edge and zoom into the same assembly floor. On ‘acetyl CoA’, a blue rectangular block stamped ‘2C PRIMER’ settles into the left clamp. On ‘Every later pair’, a second rectangular block stamped ‘2C’ travels along the lower belt toward the ACC gate. On ‘malonyl CoA’, the gate stamps that moving block ‘EXTENDER’; the short label ‘ACC’ lights above the gate. Belts and gears keep moving.
scenes.narration: In its simplest form, begin with acetyl CoA already in the cytoplasm. Its two carbons are the primer. Every later pair enters through malonyl CoA, the extender made by acetyl CoA carboxylase, or ACC.

scenes.tts: A C C combines acetyl C O A with bicarbonate and spends one A T P. The product is malonyl C O A, carrying an extra carboxyl group. Because the malonyl C O A made for synthesis has essentially one fate, this is the committed step.
scenes.caption: ACC combines acetyl CoA with bicarbonate and spends one ATP. The product is malonyl CoA, carrying an extra carboxyl group. Because the malonyl CoA made for synthesis has essentially one fate, this is the committed step.
scenes.visual: Use the same ACC gate at large scale. As each input is named, an acetyl CoA block and a small bicarbonate badge slide into separate gate slots; an ATP coin drops into a third slot and turns the crank. The output emerges as a malonyl CoA extender with the carboxyl badge visibly clipped on. On ‘committed step’, all alternate belt exits fold away, leaving one bright route toward fatty acid synthase. The gate cycles slowly after the output leaves.
scenes.narration: ACC combines acetyl CoA with bicarbonate and spends one ATP. The product is malonyl CoA, carrying an extra carboxyl group. Because the malonyl CoA made for synthesis has essentially one fate, this is the committed step.

scenes.tts: Now predict. After fatty acid synthase uses malonyl C O A, where will that newly attached carboxyl carbon end up? In the chain, or somewhere else?
scenes.caption: Now predict. After fatty acid synthase uses malonyl CoA, where will that newly attached carboxyl carbon end up? In the chain, or somewhere else?
scenes.visual: Carry the malonyl extender from the ACC gate to the mouth of the fatty acid synthase machine on the right. Make its carboxyl badge pulse yellow. Split the path ahead into two large schematic choices: the badge moving into a growing chain, or the badge leaving through an upward chute. Reveal the question ‘Where does this carbon go?’ while both arrows gently pulse and the conveyor continues moving.
scenes.narration: Now predict. After fatty acid synthase uses malonyl CoA, where will that newly attached carboxyl carbon end up? In the chain, or somewhere else?

scenes.visual: Hold the same prediction question and two choices for 4.5 seconds. The yellow carboxyl badge continues a slow pulse, the two arrows breathe alternately, and the conveyor creeps, but reveal no answer.

scenes.tts: Fatty acid synthase joins the extender to the primer. During condensation, the extra carboxyl group leaves as carbon dioxide. So little to none of a labeled bicarbonate carbon remains in palmitate.
scenes.caption: Fatty acid synthase joins the extender to the primer. During condensation, the extra carboxyl group leaves as CO₂. So little to none of a labeled bicarbonate carbon remains in palmitate.
scenes.visual: Collapse the two prediction paths into the correct upward chute. Inside the same fatty acid synthase machine, the ‘2C PRIMER’ and ‘2C EXTENDER’ blocks slide together and transform into one bar labeled ‘4C CHAIN’. Exactly as ‘leaves as carbon dioxide’ is spoken, the yellow carboxyl badge detaches and rises out as a CO2 bubble. For the labeling result, give that badge a radioactive star before it exits, then show the chain bar without any star. Gears and exhaust bubbles keep moving.
scenes.narration: Fatty acid synthase joins the extender to the primer. During condensation, the extra carboxyl group leaves as CO₂. So little to none of a labeled bicarbonate carbon remains in palmitate.

scenes.tts: That loss is useful. Joining two acetyl units directly is uphill. Releasing carbon dioxide is strongly downhill, so coupling the events pulls the new carbon-carbon bond forward. The cell spent A T P to load this molecular spring.
scenes.caption: That loss is useful. Joining two acetyl units directly is uphill. Releasing CO₂ is strongly downhill, so coupling the events pulls the new carbon–carbon bond forward. The cell spent ATP to load this molecular spring.
scenes.visual: Transform the machine’s conveyor into a large energy track marked ‘schematic’. First, two plain blocks labeled ‘acetyl’ roll toward a hill and slide backward. Then replay the ACC crank: an ATP coin compresses a visible spring beneath the malonyl extender. When the CO2 badge pops free, the spring releases and pulls the two labeled blocks together over the crest. Keep the track scrolling and the spring vibrating lightly while the conclusion lands.
scenes.narration: That loss is useful. Joining two acetyl units directly is uphill. Releasing CO₂ is strongly downhill, so coupling the events pulls the new carbon–carbon bond forward. The cell spent ATP to load this molecular spring.

scenes.tts: Condensation leaves a carbonyl that the chain cannot keep. Fatty acid synthase then finishes C R D R: reduction, dehydration, reduction. Two N A D P H supply the four electrons needed to turn that carbonyl carbon into a saturated segment.
scenes.caption: Condensation leaves a carbonyl that the chain cannot keep. Fatty acid synthase then finishes CRDR: reduction, dehydration, reduction. Two NADPH supply the four electrons needed to turn that carbonyl carbon into a saturated segment.
scenes.visual: Transform the energy track back into the same fatty acid synthase machine, now with four large stations labeled C, R, D and R around a loop. The rectangular ‘4C CHAIN’ bar carries a small text badge ‘carbonyl’, not a drawn structure. It moves through the first R, D and second R stations in order. Two green NADPH batteries enter at the two R stations and empty; at the exit, the badge transforms to ‘saturated’. The chain bar keeps circulating and each station’s wheel turns.
scenes.narration: Condensation leaves a carbonyl that the chain cannot keep. Fatty acid synthase then finishes CRDR: reduction, dehydration, reduction. Two NADPH supply the four electrons needed to turn that carbonyl carbon into a saturated segment.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. After the primer, each C R D R turn adds two carbons as one malonyl C O A. That addition costs one A T P at A C C and two N A D P H at fatty acid synthase.
scenes.caption: Here is the rule. After the primer, each CRDR turn adds two carbons as one malonyl CoA. That addition costs one ATP at ACC and two NADPH at fatty acid synthase.
scenes.visual: Zoom out to show the ACC gate feeding the same CRDR loop. One malonyl extender travels from ACC into the loop; the chain counter advances by two. Beneath it, a compact running bill updates by transformation: ‘+2 carbons’, ‘−1 ATP’, ‘−2 NADPH’. An ATP coin disappears at ACC and two NADPH batteries drain at the reduction stations. The conveyor, counter rollers and loop all continue moving.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. After the primer, each CRDR turn adds two carbons as one malonyl CoA. That addition costs one ATP at ACC and two NADPH at fatty acid synthase.

scenes.tts: The four-carbon chain returns for another turn. The same machine repeats until seven malonyl units have added fourteen carbons to the two-carbon primer. Fatty acid synthase then releases palmitate, a saturated sixteen-carbon fatty acid.
scenes.caption: The four-carbon chain returns for another turn. The same machine repeats until seven malonyl units have added fourteen carbons to the two-carbon primer. Fatty acid synthase then releases palmitate, a saturated 16-carbon fatty acid.
scenes.visual: Run the same loop as a clear time-lapse, never showing a molecular structure. One wide block labeled ‘CHAIN’ lengthens schematically while its counter advances through 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 as seven malonyl blocks enter. The ATP and NADPH meters fall in step to 7 and 14 used. At sixteen, a release arm lifts the block from the loop and stamps a large label ‘palmitate’. Ambient belts continue behind it.
scenes.narration: The four-carbon chain returns for another turn. The same machine repeats until seven malonyl units have added fourteen carbons to the two-carbon primer. Fatty acid synthase then releases palmitate, a saturated 16-carbon fatty acid.

scenes.tts: In mammals, fatty acid synthase mostly stops there. Longer chains and double bonds are handled later. So this film's rule covers the saturated chain built to palmitate. It starts from acetyl C O A already in the cytoplasm.
scenes.caption: In mammals, fatty acid synthase mostly stops there. Longer chains and double bonds are handled later. So this film’s rule covers the saturated chain built to palmitate. It starts from acetyl CoA already in the cytoplasm.
scenes.visual: Keep palmitate centered while the FAS loop continues idling behind it. On ‘mostly stops there’, a stop marker settles at counter 16. Two thin outgoing belts labeled only ‘longer later’ and ‘double bonds later’ (labels at full opacity) extend beyond the machine, but no products are drawn. A frame labeled ‘this rule’ closes around the cytoplasmic acetyl CoA input, ACC gate, CRDR loop and palmitate output.
scenes.narration: In mammals, fatty acid synthase mostly stops there. Longer chains and double bonds are handled later. So this film’s rule covers the saturated chain built to palmitate. It starts from acetyl CoA already in the cytoplasm.

scenes.tts: So the discarded carbon was never a building block. It was a temporary handle, bought with A T P, whose release drives each condensation. Count the malonyl additions, and you count both the two-carbon gains and their cost.
scenes.caption: So the discarded carbon was never a building block. It was a temporary handle, bought with ATP, whose release drives each condensation. Count the malonyl additions, and you count both the two-carbon gains and their cost.
scenes.visual: Replay the entire assembly in one continuous wide shot. For each of three quick representative turns, an ATP coin clips on a yellow carboxyl handle at ACC, the handle pops off as CO2 during condensation, two NADPH batteries drain, and the chain counter jumps by two. On ‘Count the malonyl additions’, the moving counter and cost meter align side by side, ending at seven additions, fourteen gained carbons, seven ATP and fourteen NADPH.
scenes.narration: So the discarded carbon was never a building block. It was a temporary handle, bought with ATP, whose release drives each condensation. Count the malonyl additions, and you count both the two-carbon gains and their cost.

scenes.visual: Transform the moving chain and cost meter into a clean end card while faint conveyor motion continues behind it. Show one line in large type: ‘Each two-carbon addition costs one ATP and two NADPH.’ Keep a small block labeled ‘+2C’ sliding once from left to right beneath the line.
